About the Role

Groww has started a bonds business, with distribution through the Groww app. We are now building a bond desk that acquires bond inventory on Groww’s balance sheet. As Senior Manager, you will set up the desk’s credit underwriting from the ground up: deciding which issuers and bonds Groww is willing to hold, at what price and size, and how we keep watching them after we buy.

This is a founding role with direct ownership of credit risk decisions and the chance to build a risk engine that sees beyond the rating.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Area What you will do
Set up the bond desk
  • Design the end-to-end process for sourcing, evaluating, pricing and acquiring bonds onto Groww’s balance sheet
  • Draft the credit policy, delegation of authority and exposure limits (issuer, group, sector, rating bucket, tenor) with Risk, Treasury, Legal and Compliance
Underwrite issuers
  • Run full credit assessment of financial issuers (NBFCs, HFCs, MFIs) and non-financial issuers (corporates, real estate, infrastructure, structured and securitised paper)
  • Cover rating rationale, financials and balance-sheet health, asset quality and credit losses, liquidity and ALM, payment track record, default history and the issuer’s ecosystem and sponsor strength
  • Make a clear approve, limit or reject recommendation with a written credit note
Build the risk engine
  • Create an in-house risk framework that assesses risk beyond published agency ratings: scorecards by issuer type, early-warning indicators, red-flag and knock-out rules, and benchmarks against peers
  • Partner with data and engineering teams to automate ratio computation, filing and news monitoring, and use AI tools for document review while keeping judgment with the credit team
Recurring due diligence
  • Run periodic reviews of every approved issuer and every bond held, covering results, rating actions, covenants, trustee reports and payment status
  • Hold management meetings and diligence calls, and visit issuers’ offices or field operations where needed
  • Trigger watch-list, limit reduction or exit actions on early signs of stress
Pricing and inventory
  • Recommend entry yield and spread against G-sec and AAA benchmarks, and cross-check pricing on other bond platforms and the secondary market
  • Manage concentration, liquidity and holding period of the inventory, and plan the exit route for each position
Governance and reporting
  • Present to the credit committee and maintain a full audit trail for each decision
  • Report portfolio quality, exposures and watch-list items to senior leadership
Market and regulatory insight
  • Track India’s changing credit landscape: sector cycles, RBI and SEBI developments, funding conditions and new issuer segments
  • Build relationships with rating agencies, debenture trustees, arrangers and issuer management
Build the team
  • Hire and mentor credit analysts as the desk scales

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Requirement Detail
Underwriting experience More than 6 years underwriting bond issuers across financial and non-financial companies, in a bank, NBFC, AMC, insurer, rating agency or credit fund
India credit landscape Extensive knowledge of how India’s credit market is changing, including NBFC and HFC regulation, retail and unsecured lending cycles, sector stress points and issuer behaviour in downturns
Financial and non-financial risk Deep understanding of financial risk (leverage, liquidity, asset quality, cash flows) and non-financial risk (governance, promoter conduct, regulatory standing, group structure, fraud and concentration)
Risk engine capability Able to design and run a proprietary risk framework that goes beyond agency ratings, and to explain where and why the view differs from the rating
Recurring due diligence Proven discipline in ongoing monitoring and periodic issuer reviews, not only one-time approvals
Documents and structures Comfortable reading information memoranda, trust deeds, security and covenant terms, and securitisation structures
Communication and ownership Writes sharp credit notes, defends recommendations to committees and senior leadership, and works independently to build a function from scratch

GOOD TO HAVE

  • Extensive hands-on experience underwriting bonds specifically (NCDs, debentures and securitised paper), beyond general loan or credit underwriting
  • Experience with securitisation, pass-through certificates and co-lending exposures
  • Experience working with SEBI NCS regulations, RBI NBFC scale-based regulation and debenture trustee processes
  • Experience setting up a new desk, credit function or risk framework
  • Knowledge of bond pricing, yield curves and secondary market liquidity in India

QUALIFICATIONS

  • CA, MBA (Finance) or equivalent; CFA or FRM is an advantage

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THE FIRST 12 MONTHS

  • Credit policy, limits and approval process approved and running
  • First issuer universe underwritten, with credit notes and limits in place
  • In-house risk scorecard live, and reviewed against agency ratings
  • Recurring review cycle running for every approved issuer and held bond
  • Underwriting team hired and trained to run the desk’s pipeline

Description

Alexa Proactive, now powered by Alexa+, brings customers personalized, proactive content, suggestions and actions across Alexa devices and surfaces: news, sports, recipes, music, shopping deals and tips to discover new features. Behind these experiences are recommendation and ranking systems that anticipate what customers need and surface the right content, suggestions, or actions at the right moment, through the right channel. Deciding what to show, to whom, when, and through which channel, for millions of customers, is a large-scale recommendation and ranking problem, and much of its science is still ahead of us.

We are looking for a Senior Applied Scientist to join ML Engineering (MLE) India in Bengaluru, part of the Personalization and Delivery Engineering (PDE) org in Alexa AI, and build the recommendation and ranking systems behind Alexa+ proactive experiences. You will be part of Proactive Science, a global science team across time zones, and set the scientific direction for your area: content retrieval and relevance, ranking and re-ranking, how the full page is composed, and how the system learns from customer feedback. You will work closely with Proactive Science partners and with the software and data engineers who run these systems in production.

We value scientists who can move fast: iterate on algorithms quickly, validate ideas through rigorous online experiments, and turn them into measurable customer and business impact. As a senior scientist, you will frame ambiguous problems on your own, make sound trade-offs between model quality, latency and cost, and deliver end-to-end solutions to production with limited guidance. You will also mentor scientists and engineers, and influence engineering, product, and science partners across teams.

Key job responsibilities

• Science roadmap: Own the science roadmap for proactive recommendation and ranking. Turn customer and business goals into clear ML problems, plans and metrics.
• Proactive recommendation and ranking: Design and scale multi-stage recommendation systems (candidate generation, relevance filtering, ranking, re-ranking, and delivery policy) that decide what to surface, to whom, when, and through which channel, for millions of customers across Alexa devices and surfaces.
• Personalization: Move ranking from popularity to deep personalization, using customer interests, engagement history, context (time of day, device) and content understanding. Apply two-tower retrieval, cross-encoders, learning-to-rank, CTR/CVR prediction, and sequential and multi-task recommendation models.
• Whole-page optimization: Optimize the whole page, not only the ranked list: slot rules, diversity, share of voice and backup content.
• Objective design and alignment: Build multi-objective ranking and optimization frameworks that align model objectives with business goals and customer experience metrics, with guardrails against fatigue, dismissals and repeated content.
• Rapid iteration to impact: Drive fast experimentation cycles from hypothesis to offline evaluation, online A/B testing, and launch. Continuously improve models based on customer feedback and online results.
• Explore and exploit: Bring explore and exploit into the system through contextual bandits, counterfactual and off-policy evaluation.
• ML foundations: Partner with software and data engineers to build a feature store shared by training and inference, feature data-quality checks, automated retraining with evaluation gates, and model performance dashboards (CTR, NDCG and business metrics).
• Content understanding and generation: Use LLMs and embeddings to strengthen content understanding, topic tagging and representations for ranking, and contribute to the generation of proactive content.
• Scientific rigor: Own the full science lifecycle with sound experiment design, counterfactual evaluation, and production accountability. Ship models within strict latency and cost budgets, with safe fallbacks (for example distillation and efficient inference).
• Leadership: Mentor scientists and engineers, run science and design reviews, write clear documents for senior leaders, raise the hiring bar, and build reusable science components across teams.

A day in the life

A DAY IN THE LIFE

No two days look the same, because many of the hardest problems are still open. You might start the morning with A/B results for a personalized re-ranker: clicks went up, but so did dismissals. You decide how to balance the two before you dial it up. Next, you take on a cold-start problem: a new content provider has no engagement history, so how should it earn a slot without hurting the page? With Proactive Science partners across time zones, you shape next half's roadmap: move from popularity ranking to deep personalization, replace fixed slot rules with a learned whole-page policy, add explore and exploit, and make retraining automatic. With software and data engineers, you work out how a larger model fits a tight latency budget, and what safe fallback serves when it times out. You end the day writing a short proposal that turns one open question into a plan the team can build.

About The Team

ML Engineering (MLE) India, part of Personalization and Delivery Engineering (PDE) in Alexa AI, builds the personalization and proactive-intelligence systems that let Alexa anticipate what customers need before they ask. In Bengaluru, we own the AERO runtime, which selects and composes proactive content for Alexa devices, and CxT (Customer Experience Telemetry), which captures how customers see and engage with that content. Together with Proactive Science, our global science team, we turn this into better proactive experiences for customers.

• Shape the science: you set the roadmap, pick the problems, and define how science and engineering work together on proactive experiences.
• A direct path to customers: our team runs the system that serves your models, and our telemetry gives you the signals you learn from. You see the impact of your work in weeks, not years.
• Global scope, local ownership: work with Proactive Science scientists across time zones and with the PES ranking and PCGS content teams, while you own your problem space end to end.
• Ship and publish: we support publications at top venues (KDD, RecSys, WWW, SIGIR, WSDM, NeurIPS, ICML) while making sure your research reaches production.

We value ownership, high standards, fast iteration and working backwards from the customer.

Basic Qualifications

• PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience
• Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc.
• Experience with large scale distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark etc.

About the role
0G is hiring its first dedicated DevOps engineer to own our cloud platform end to end: infrastructure, deployments, networking, security hygiene and cost. Today that work is spread across several developers.
Our platform runs on five providers: Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, AWS, Cloudflare and Vercel. It includes:
• 
Validator, seed, RPC, and archive nodes for our mainnet and testnet
• 
Confidential-computing (TEE) workloads, GPU machines and storage nodes
• 
Kubernetes clusters and managed databases
• 
A global RPC load balancer at the edge, and our web apps
All together, that is more than 200 virtual machines. You will be the person who knows what runs where, why it runs there, and what it costs.

What you'll own
You own the platform, from the network edge to the bill.
• 
Cloud operations: provisioning, upgrades, capacity and the full resource lifecycle on Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud and AWS. That includes rightsizing and releasing what nobody uses.
• 
Kubernetes: run, upgrade and scale our clusters. Keep them on supported versions and design node pools, autoscaling and Spot capacity.
• 
Blockchain node fleet: operate validator, sentry, seed, RPC and archive nodes, including peering topology, snapshots, sync and client upgrades.
• 
Networking and edge: VPC design, load balancers, DNS, Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and WAF, and keeping internet egress deliberate and cheap.
• 
Infrastructure as code and CI/CD: every environment defined in Terraform or Pulumi. You design and run CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent such as GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, covering builds, tests, security scans and releases from commit to production, with no manual steps.
• 
Observability and on-call: metrics, logs, alerts and dashboards, including control of metric cardinality. You also run incident response and write the postmortems.
• 
Security and access: least-privilege IAM across every provider, secrets management, and no databases or admin ports open to the internet.
• 
Cost management: billing exports, budgets and alerts, tagging, a monthly cost review and commitment planning.
• 
Developer enablement: templates, preview environments, documentation and support for the engineers who ship on the platform.
Our stack
Kubernetes: GKE, EKS, Helm, Ingress and Gateway API, autoscaling, RBAC, network policies
Networking: TCP/IP, subnets and CIDR, routing, NAT, L4 and L7 load balancers, DNS, TLS, firewalls, VPC peering
Google Cloud: Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud SQL, Cloud Run, IAM, Cloud Monitoring, billing export to BigQuery
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Pulumi
CI/CD and containers: Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), Argo CD, Docker and BuildKit, container registries
Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Cloud Monitoring, CloudWatch, Alibaba CloudMonitor
Linux: Systems administration, systemd, disks and filesystems, performance debugging
Alibaba Cloud: ECS, VPC, NLB and ALB, ESSD disks, RDS, PolarDB, SAE, Cloud Firewall
AWS: EC2, EKS, RDS, ALB and NLB, Route 53, S3, Organizations
Cloudflare: DNS, Workers, Tunnels, WAF and rate limiting, Zero Trust
Databases (operations): PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, managed Kafka
Blockchain nodes: CometBFT-based chains, reth and other EVM clients, P2P networking
Vercel: Projects, builds, ISR, team access
Confidential computing: Intel TDX virtual machines on Google Cloud and Alibaba Cloud

Must-haves
• 
We want 5+ years in DevOps, SRE or platform roles, including 3+ years running production Kubernetes and owning CI/CD pipelines.
Kubernetes, in depth
• 
Upgrading control planes and node pools with no downtime, and keeping clusters on supported versions.
• 
Scheduling: requests and limits, affinity, taints and tolerations, priority, and eviction under node pressure.
• 
Autoscaling with the HPA, cluster autoscaler or Karpenter, plus Spot or preemptible node pools for non-critical work.
• 
Networking inside the cluster: CNI, Services, Ingress or Gateway API, network policies, and DNS within the cluster.
• 
Security: RBAC, Pod Security, workload identity, and secrets that never sit in plain environment variables.
• 
Stateful workloads: StatefulSets, persistent volumes and CSI drivers, and backup and restore.
• 
Packaging and delivery with Helm or Kustomize, ideally through GitOps with Argo CD or Flux.
• 
Debugging a failing pod, node or rollout from events, logs and metrics.
CI/CD, in depth
• 
Pipeline design: you have built and run production CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Tekton). Pipelines are defined as code in a Jenkinsfile or workflow YAML, with shared libraries and reusable templates.
• 
CI platform operations: running Jenkins controllers with ephemeral agents on Kubernetes, or self-hosted runners. That includes plugin and version upgrades, credential handling, and scaling build capacity.
• 
Build pipelines: multi-service and monorepo builds with caching and parallel stages, and versioned artifacts. Container images built with Docker, BuildKit or Kaniko, including multi-architecture images, image scanning, SBOMs and signing.
• 
Deployment pipelines: promotion from dev to staging to production with approvals and quality gates, plus blue-green, canary and fast rollback. GitOps with Argo CD or Flux, and database migrations as part of a release.
• 
Infrastructure pipelines: Terraform or Pulumi plan and apply from CI, with policy checks and drift detection.
• 
Pipeline security: short-lived credentials through OIDC federation or a secrets vault instead of long-lived keys, least-privilege deploy roles, and protected branches.
• 
Release engineering for our chain: building and publishing node binaries and images, and coordinating rolling upgrades across validator and RPC fleets.
• 
Delivery health: you track build time, build cost, flaky tests and DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore), and you cut wasted builds with ignore rules and caching.
Networking fundamentals
• 
TCP/IP, subnetting and CIDR, routing, NAT, and the difference between L4 and L7 load balancing.
• 
DNS, TLS and certificates, firewalls and security groups.
• 
Private connectivity: VPC design, peering, private endpoints, and keeping internal traffic off public IPs.
• 
Troubleshooting with dig, curl, mtr and tcpdump, and understanding what internet egress costs.
Also required
• 
Production experience on at least two of Google Cloud, AWS and Alibaba Cloud, and willingness to learn the third quickly.
• 
Terraform or Pulumi in production, plus scripting in Bash and in Python or Go.
• 
A track record of cutting a cloud bill with data, through rightsizing, cleanup or commitments.
• 
A security-first habit with production credentials, and clear written communication.
Nice to have
• 
Running blockchain nodes in production, such as CometBFT validators and sentries, EVM archive or RPC nodes, and snapshot pipelines.
• 
Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and Zero Trust at scale.
• 
Alibaba Cloud on the international site, including its billing and support model.
• 
Confidential computing (Intel TDX) and GPU workloads.
• 
CKA or CKS certification, a FinOps certification, or experience moving a team between CI systems, such as Jenkins to GitHub Actions.
• 
Go or Rust, enough to read and patch the services you operate.
